title: Varied Grips - B
texts:
Finger strength will vary between different grip positions. It is important to change the load between each grip type in order to maintain the correct intensity. For example, 4 finger half crimp will likely be stronger than front 3 open drag. Therefore, reduce the load used between these two grip positions. 

The goal of this workout is to improve finger strength in different grip positions. This will be achieve through becoming more accustomed to each grip position and through increasing the load over time. In this workout complete each hang at an intensity that is challenging but manageable and feels safe. We recommend using 8/10 on the RPE. This equates to 8/10 for effort, 10 being maximal/failure and 0 being no effort at all. Please refer to the RPE scale for more details. Please remember 8/10 in one grip position may be a different load to 8/10 in another grip position. 

Increase the intensity beyond body weight by adding additional load around your waist via a harness. You can reduce the load below body weight by using the assistance of a pulley, foothold or theraband. You can also increase the size of hold used to decrease the intensity. 

Sets 1-3: 4 Finger grip half crimp or open hand
Sets 4-5: Front 3 half crimp
Sets 6-7: Back 3 half crimp
Sets 8-10: Front 3 open drag

Rate of perceived exertion (RPE)

RPE is a quantitative measure of a person’s perception of effort during sport and exercise. Crimpd uses RPE to determine the effort it takes to complete one set of given workouts. If a workout requires an RPE of 3, this equates to a perceived effort of 3 out of 10. 

10 – Maximal effort and often failure to complete more than one set of a workout at this intensity. 
9 – Close to maximal effort for each set of a workout. 
8 – High effort levels needed.
7 – Manageable but challenging, a reasonable high effort is required. 
6 – Moderate intensity with a moderate to high effort needed.
5 – Moderate effort required to complete each set.
4 – Low to moderate effort levels needed. 
3 – Very low effort levels. 
2 – Minimal effort needed
1 – Hardly any effort at all
0 – No effort
